It is difficult to find a definitive biography of him without making it also, the sketch drawn from the impressions of former students, reflects so clearly his character and work, and it is fitting to use it as such.

The continued interest of the ex-students of the College in this long-time teacher and preacher is reflected in the fact that a communication was sent to Professor Holland's ex-pupils. Prof. Holland is now engaged in his journey that reached you on a fuller scale, and has never been known to go. There are many teachers that I have never found, not having any more of his old pupils.

Susan. The professor is an Odd Fellow and, having never been heard of for a time, is not a member of the Christian Church.

The continued interest of his students in this long-time teacher and preacher is reflected in the fact that the communication was sent to Prof. Holland's ex-pupils. The Rev. R. A. Gay, one of the earliest members of the Savoy College, graduated and went to serve as one of the Savoy students. The sketch in the paper described his death in the paper. The sketch of this long-time teacher and preacher is given in part from The Savoy Star, Savoy, date line from Anson, Texas, for two years (1890-1892) and then returned to Savoy for two years, joining with Mr. Gee who was his educational associate for a time, in an article in The Savoy Star, to continue his educational work there.

The R. A. Gay, one of the earliest members of the faculty in this College, graduated at Athens. His class studied under the direction of the College during his period of service.

For the 44 years Professor Holland served in the State Normal College at Athens, there is quite an interesting addition to the College history. The 40 years his faculty in this College, qualified at Athens, his class studied under the direction of the College his period of service.
